components.boundary: Actionable option; prerequisite is CNSW-SNW Option 1 (Hunter Transmission Project), a separate project
components.description: Power flow control devices installed in the 330 kV network supplying Sydney from the south, improving flow sharing between the northern and southern CNSW-SNW segments.
New 330 kV South Creek switching station cutting into Sydney West – Bayswater (#32), Sydney West – Regentville (#38) and Bannaby – Sydney West (#39).

components.description: Rebuild 7 km of existing single-circuit 330 kV between South Creek and Sydney West as double-circuit, strung with HTLS conductor.

components.boundary: Works on existing lines; not new trunk route
components.description: Re-conductor approx. 7 km of existing double-circuit 330 kV lines 32 and 38 with HTLS conductor between South Creek and Sydney West.

Two new 330 kV line switch bays at Bannaby, one new 330 kV line switch bay at Sydney West, two new 500 kV line switch bays at Bannaby, and re-termination of 500 kV designed lines at Bannaby and South Creek.

Upgrade South Creek to a 330/500 kV substation with separate 500 kV and 330 kV yards linked by underground cable, cutting into 500 kV Eraring – Kemps Creek (#5A1, #5A2), with three 1,500 MVA 500/330 kV transformers.
Four 120 MVAr line shunt reactors on the 500 kV lines between Bannaby and South Creek. No synchronous condensers appear in the archived scope.

findings.evidence: The archived ODP delivers both stages of the 500 kV option in the 2033-34 financial year; Transgrid's own PADR confirms the same 2033/34 earliest in-service timing for Option 6's 500 kV transmission line (Stage 2), with Stage 1 (South Creek substation and power flow control) timed at 2030/31. The chart's 2034 is the author's calendar proxy and ignores the earlier Stage 1 timing.

The immutable chart contains $3.5bn, consistent with rounding the PADR Option 6 total of $3,519m nominal to one decimal billion. The source gives Stage 1 $1,135m and Stage 2 $2,384m, P50 Class 5 (+100%/-50%). AEMO's $2,621m modelled $2025 amount is a different price basis. No transcription error is established (PADR p38; AEMO 2026 p43).
findings.supported_value: 3.519 AUD billion nominal, combined Option 6 stages; P50 Class 5 (+100%/-50%); rounds to original 3.5

findings.evidence: Transgrid's own PADR states that Option 6, once complete (both stages), adds 3.6 GW of transfer capacity to the network supplying Sydney, Newcastle and Wollongong from the south -- the same combined Option 6 boundary the chart represents. AEMO separately states 3,600 MW forward capacity for the 500 kV transmission option alone (and 0 MW for the power flow control option).

findings.evidence: Transgrid's June 2023 Southern Ring preparatory-activities document, now archived, states the new Bannaby-South Creek 500 kV double-circuit overhead line has an approximate length of 114 km, matching the chart exactly. However, Transgrid's later 2026 PADR instead describes the (differently scoped) Bannaby-South Western Sydney 500 kV line as extending to around 100 km, so the chart's figure reflects an earlier preparatory estimate, not the current PADR boundary.

findings.evidence: 30.70175438596491 = 3,500 AUD million / 114 km, using the original chart inputs. The $3.5bn rounds the $3,519m nominal Option 6 estimate; the 114 km is the older 2023 preparatory route, whereas the 2026 PADR describes approximately 100 km on a revised scope. This mixed-vintage ratio is not a reconciled source-defined construction cost per km (2023 preparatory p8; PADR pp38,43).
